newsitem.title: USA: March Clinton-Yeltsin summit planned for Helsinki.
newsitem.headline: March Clinton-Yeltsin summit planned for Helsinki.

text.p: U.S. President Bill Clinton and Russian President Boris Yeltsin have chosen Helsinki as the site for a summit in March, U.S. officials said on Friday.
In Helsinki, Finnish radio said the meeting would take place on March 19 and 20, possibly continuing to March 21.

The U.S. officials said the site and date were agreed upon during meetings between Vice President Al Gore and Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin, who are conferring as part of a periodic U.S.-Russia liaison effort.
They were to announce the details at a news conference scheduled for 11:30 a.m. EST (1630 GMT), the officials said.

It is Yeltsin's turn to visit the United States, since Clinton went to Moscow for the last summit in April. But the White House was flexible on that point and amenable to Russian suggestions the summit be moved to a third country closer to Russia because of Yeltsin's health.
He is recovering from heart bypass surgery and pneumonia.
In Moscow, Itar-Tass news agency on Friday quoted Kremlin spokesman Sergei Yastrzhembsky as saying Yeltsin was considering requesting a change of summit venue to Europe.
He cancelled a visit to the Netherlands earlier this month and is under doctors' orders to limit his workload.

Yeltsin was shown on television on Thursday addressing the nation directly for the first time since his release from hospital on January 20 after treatment for pneumonia. He spoke for less than a minute on a pension controversy.
His voice was steady, his speech slow and his manner determined, but he had clearly aged considerably since a quintuple heart bypass operation in November.
Finnish diplomatic officials said Finland was happy to welcome the two leaders, having played host to a summit in 1990 between then-President George Bush and then-Soviet President Mikhail Gorbachev.
